newsitem.title: USA: Dlr sags quietly at noon as crosses dominate in US.
newsitem.headline: Dlr sags quietly at noon as crosses dominate in US.

text.p: The dollar settled a touch lower at midday after getting crossed signals from a buoyant mark/yen and sterling/mark during the session, dealers said.
Before mild profit taking set in, the mark extended its overnight rise to 67.11 yen in New York, nudging dollar/mark briefly below 1.72 and supporting dollar/yen.

"It's trying to explore down there on back of mark/yen but I think if you see 1.7170 or 80 marks its just as good a buy. I don't think this thing is falling out of bed," said John Barlow, a senior dealer at Bayerische Landesbank Girozentrale.
"It's more likely that dollar/yen will continue to move up with the mark/yen than dollar/mark move down," he continued.
Mark strength was counterbalanced, and the dollar supported to some degree, by the pound's rise to a new 59-month high above 2.87 marks, dealers said.
The dollar was tethered to opening levels of 1.7210/20 marks and 115.30/40 yen for most of the session. It eased to 1.7195/05 marks -- its second foray below 1.72 -- and to 115.20/30 yen at noon.
Dollar/mark experienced little follow-through selling, although dealers expected stop-loss orders below 1.72.
Dollar/yen was unable to translate its overnight gains into a break above its early peak of 115.67. Talk of Japanese offers by 116 curbed enthusiasm, dealers said.

The dollar powered above 115 yen in Asia after the Group of Seven (G7) nations refrained from serious finger wagging over Japan's huge trade surplus, with only cursory mention in the joint statement at the conclusion of the weekend summit.

"I really don't see much breaking loose today at all, the G7 turned out to be somewhat of a non-event," said Stephen Flanagan, a vice president of corporate foreign exchange at Credit Agricole Paribas.
The G7 said Japan needs to spur strong domestic-led growth, avoid a significant increase in its external surplus and enact structural deregulation and economic reforms.
The leaders also asked their finance ministers to cooperate closely on economic policy and in exchange markets.
Evidence of healthy Japanese growth has been scant and the future of dollar/yen may be mapped out by Japan's quarterly Tankan report on business conditions, due at 2350 GMT Tuesday.
"The Tankan is expected to be a little bit on the weaker side and I think that's probably aiding a weaker yen as people trade ahead of it," Flanagan said.
Cable was dragged up to a five-month high above $1.67, lifted along with Sterling/mark's lurch to 2.8725 and the prospect of higher interest rates in Britain.
But some dealers expressed caution that the pound's technical rally may be overdone and in need of a breather.
"The (daily) RSI in cable is at its highest level for the whole year," said a dealer at a European Bank in New York.
At noon, the pound stood at $1.6690/00, up from $1.6625/35 at the open. Dollar/Swiss was unchanged at 1.4322/32.
The dollar eased to Canadian $1.3889/94 from C$1.3893/98.
((--Alden Bentley, 212 859 1667))
